 COLUMN: Add another ‘prison of hope’ to Indiana women’s basketball’s depth this season
 Freshman guard GiGi Battle dribbles the ball across the court in a game against Southern Illinois University on Nov. 6, 2026, at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall in Bloomington. The Hoosiers recorded 41 bench points.
 Photo by Manasvi Doshi 
 / The Indiana Daily Student
 By
 Sean McAvoy 
 Nov 7, 2026 12:23 am 
 · Updated Nov 7, 2026 12:23 am 
 There’s a patented saying in sports: “It’s the hope that kills you.”   
 This rang true for Indiana women’s basketball last season, as the Hoosiers missed the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2018.   
 But after the Cream and Crimson’s 79-50 victory over Florida Gulf Coast University on Tuesday to open the 2026-27 campaign, Indiana head coach Teri Moren stated a different testament about her team.   
 “I'm a prisoner of hope,” Moren said postgame.   
 It’s a prison that I, for one, would lock myself in after the Hoosiers’ 96-55 drubbing over Southern Illinois University on Friday night at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall in Bloomington.   
 The Hoosiers received a balanced scoring attack from up-and-down their lineup. Redshirt junior guard Lenée Beaumont led the way with only 14 points, even after exiting the game late in the second quarter following a hard and awkward fall before returning in the third frame.   
 In total, six Indiana players finished with double digits and four others contributed at least single digit scoring totals on the court.   
 The scoring production has come from every single player in the lineup. It doesn’t matter if they’re a freshman or senior, a guard or forward a transfer or returnee. Indiana has been clinical on the offensive end of the court.   
 It bodes well for the Hoosiers to swing back in the opposite direction after last year’s offense mostly came from one source: senior guard Shay Ciezki.   
 It’s no secret that Indiana has depth this season.   
 Moren had to change her approach during the offseason when partaking in the transfer portal. Last season’s transfer portal class was marred by unproven commodities that had potential but were just too young to reach the standard that Indiana needed them to play at.   
 That style of transfer portal business resulted in 14 losses by the end of the season.   
 This offseason, Moren and her staff had a much better approach to how they acquired talent in the transfer portal. Two former Big Ten players, plus two others who played multiple years at the high-major level.   
 When looking at Friday’s box score, the addition of those experienced players stood out as an aspect of Indiana’s offense that I believe won’t go away as the team ventures further into the season and faces tougher opponents.   
 Fifth-year guard Kenzie Hare knocked down three 3-pointers in the starting lineup. Senior forward Jess Petire had seven points off the bench. Fifth-year forward Alisa Williams turned in another impressive effort as the backup post player to junior forward Zania Socka-Nguemen. And senior guard Malia Samuels had five points and five assists.   
 Those aren’t eye-popping stats that would make the headlines at ESPN tomorrow morning, but they’re stats that lead to winning basketball.   
 “We've already proven that we have so many threats on our team, not even just the starting five,” sophomore forward Maya Makalusky said postgame. “And I think that’s a threat to all the teams that we play in the future.”   
 It’s easier to take this performance with a grain of salt than the season opener. At least Florida Gulf Coast was projected as one of the contenders in the Atlantic Sun Conference. Southern Illinois, on the other hand, lost to Division II University of Illinois Springfield on Tuesday.   
 I’m no connoisseur of Division II women’s basketball, but I’m in the mind to believe that it might be the worst loss any Indiana opponent will have this season.   
 The games will get tougher — obviously — and depth might shrink as the season continues. But you might see new players step into roles that didn’t come natural at the beginning of the season.   
 Moren has always talked about any freshman collegiate basketball player’s shortcomings on the defensive side of the ball. It’s the reason she hasn’t played a lot of them during her time coaching at Indiana.   
 But there’s one skill Indiana’s three freshmen have shown to start this season — hustle.   
 Guard GiGi Battle dove to the floor to fight for a loose ball in the Hoosiers’ exhibition win over Marian University. Forward Addy Nyemchek and guard Ashlinn James did the same deep into the fourth quarter Friday.   
 While rarely a game-altering play, it’s a trait that Indiana lacked last season.   
 “It's a great luxury to have, but this thing is far from being over,” Moren said about her team’s depth postgame. “For these freshmen, I think they're getting really, really great minutes and experience playing.”   
 Indiana’s bench group, including the three freshmen, finished the game with 41 points. It’s the highest since tallying 45 against Bellarmine University on Dec. 15, 2024. The closest total last season was 18 points against Iowa State University on Nov. 30, 2025, a game the Hoosiers scored 95 points in.   
 You can detract from Friday’s results by saying it was an early nonconference game against lower-tier opponents. I’ll disagree with you because we never saw Indiana look like this against those kinds of opponents last season.   
 Indiana still has a lot of regular season left to go — 28 games, to be exact — but I’ll be locked away in Moren’s hope-filled prison. The Cream and Crimson have the kind of depth that wins many more games after Friday.
